chunks: And from him, from Abdullah ibn Bahri, from Dawud ibn Ali al-Ya'qubi, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about the sick person who is unable to throw the jamarat, so he said: 'It is thrown on his behalf.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a sick person who cannot throw the jamarat during Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies the concession (*rukhsa*) for those physically unable to perform *rami al-jamarat*, permitting a proxy to throw the stones on their behalf. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the obligation of Hajj acts is tied to physical capacity, ensuring that illness does not invalidate the pilgrimage. It highlights the balance between strict ritual adherence and divine mercy in Shia fiqh.
